why: Tried to refute on all three axes and could not. Read the WHOLE line — it is a three-sentence line and the other two REINFORCE the claim ('Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start.' / 'Claude keeps `MEMORY.md` concise by moving detailed notes into separate topic files.'). :30 restates it in the comparison table ('Every session (first 200 lines or 25KB)'), :386 adds the post-write measurement against 'the 200-line and 25KB read limits', and :390 scopes it ('This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length'), which is the one qualifier that could have refuted this and does not — see (3). (2) CITED FILES: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-32 is `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` = `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — a line slice, no byte check. capabilities/materializer.ts:181 is `const content = readFileSync(contentPath);` inside `readText` (169-186), a whole-file read returned at :186 with no cap. base-agent.ts `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (~976-1014) does `for (const layer of runtime.view.memory) { const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource); ... }` and pushes `content` verbatim into `<capability-layer>` bodies; the cited 989-1006 window is the rule-parse/import-strip tail of that same loop (the `readText` call itself sits a few lines above at ~977), so the line range is loose by ~12 lines but points at the right function and the right loop. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, both directions. Live-path claim CONFIRMED end to end: prompts/system.ts:453-455 `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, and `capabilityContextPinned` is positional arg 12 of `getSystemPrompt`, passed as `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` by BOTH live backends (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256). So whenever the capability runtime is active — the normal turn — the 200-line `readMemoryFile` composer is skipped entirely and MEMORY.md rides the uncapped pinned path. `rg -na 'MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT|readMemoryFile'` over packages/ apps/ (with -a; native-sources.ts does carry NUL bytes) returns exactly three non-test consumers: memory-store.ts itself, the legacy `loadMemoryPromptBlock` chain, and capabilities/native-sources.ts:427, the `@import` scan — which matches the claim's last sentence precisely. The only test asserting the cap (memory-store.test.ts:47 'caps prompt reads to 200 lines') tests `readMemoryFile` directly, i.e. the dead branch. Byte-cap claim CONFIRMED: no 25KB constant exists on the memory path; the only instruction byte cap in the repo is MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 (capabilities/native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), and that is the SIBLING subsystem — lazily discovered nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction files, never a MEMORY.md memory layer. (I nearly missed that constant by piping a grep through `head -30`, the exact trap AGENTS.md warns about.) The doc's :390 carve-out does not rescue us either: this fork's MEMORY.md is the auto-memory index, not a CLAUDE.md analogue — the `remember` session tool appends agent-written entries stamped `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` to session/project/user MEMORY.md (session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:21-49) and a scheduled auto-memory cleanup pass ages them out, while human project instructions live in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md on the separate nested-instruction path. The fork also already carries the 200-line constant lifted from this very page, so matching this limit was the intent, not an out-of-scope Claude-ism. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 — the only memory-adjacent row there is PiPendingApprovalV1.requestedAt, unrelated. Not a rebrand, gateway, or dropped-subscription product difference. Two imprecisions that do not refute: the pinned block is not literally 'the system prompt' on the Claude backend (it rides the pinned context block, not `presetAppend`), and the same uncapped read applies to `.agents/rules` layers, which the claim does not mention.
correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with the live path worse than the doc gap alone implies. No 25KB byte cap exists anywhere on the memory path. `readMemoryFile` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:29-32) slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines with no byte check, but it is reachable only from the LEGACY composer: prompts/system.ts:453-455 calls `loadMemoryPromptBlock` solely when `capabilityContextPinned` is false, and both live backends pass `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` for that argument (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256). On the live route every `runtime.view.memory` layer — project/user/session MEMORY.md and the `.agents/rules` files — is read whole by capabilities/materializer.ts:169-186 `readText` and pushed verbatim into the pinned capability block by `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (base-agent.ts ~976-1014), so neither the 200-line nor the 25KB limit is enforced on any turn that runs the capability runtime. The 200-line cap survives only in the legacy fallback composer, in the `@import` scan at capabilities/native-sources.ts:427, and in the one test that calls `readMemoryFile` directly. The repo's only instruction byte cap, MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 (capabilities/native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), governs lazily discovered nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files and never MEMORY.md.
